title: Cult films
description: Directors, famous scenes and twists, from Hitchcock to The Matrix.

content.title: Lights, camera, action
content.body: Hitchcock thrillers, mind-bending science fiction and Tarantino dialogue: these questions are about films that people still talk about. No big spoilers, but a few famous twists are mentioned!

content.question: In In Time (2011), what is used as money?

choices.text: The time people have left to live

content.explanation: People stop ageing at 25; after that, every second must be earned and paid for. When the clock on your arm reaches zero, you die.

content.question: In Time was directed by Andrew Niccol. Which other film on this list did he direct?
content.explanation: Niccol wrote and directed Gattaca (1997), another story about a society that sorts people, this time by their genes.

content.question: Where does the title Gattaca come from?

choices.text: The letters G, A, T and C, the four bases of DNA
The name of the director's dog

content.explanation: Guanine, adenine, thymine and cytosine. In the film, people are judged by their DNA, and Vincent, born without genetic selection, fights to go to space.

content.question: In Inception (2010), what object does Cobb use as a totem to check whether he is dreaming?
content.explanation: If the top keeps spinning forever, he is in a dream. The famous last shot of Christopher Nolan's film ends before we know whether it falls.

content.question: Which famous line does the little boy Cole whisper in The Sixth Sense (1999)?
content.explanation: The film by M. Night Shyamalan is famous for its final twist. The other lines come from The Terminator, The Shining and Star Wars.

content.question: In Pulp Fiction, Vincent explains that in France, a Quarter Pounder with Cheese is called...
content.explanation: "They got the metric system, they wouldn't know what the... a Quarter Pounder is." Quentin Tarantino's film won the Palme d'Or at Cannes in 1994.

content.question: In Dark City (1998), what happens every night at midnight?

choices.text: Time stops, everyone falls asleep, and mysterious Strangers reshape the city and people's memories
The sun rises in the west
All the lights go out for one minute and nothing else happens

content.explanation: In Alex Proyas's film, the hero is the only one who stays awake. Its themes of a fake reality came out one year before a very famous film...

content.question: In The Matrix (1999), Morpheus offers Neo two pills. Which one shows him the truth?

choices.text: Neither: the truth is in a phone call

content.explanation: "You take the blue pill, the story ends... You take the red pill, you stay in Wonderland." The film was made by the Wachowskis.

content.question: In Stardust (2007), Tristan goes to find a fallen star. What is the star?

choices.text: A glowing rock that grants wishes

content.explanation: Adapted from Neil Gaiman's novel, the film also features Robert De Niro as the surprising Captain Shakespeare, the captain of a flying pirate ship.

content.question: What do Cloud Atlas (2012) and The Matrix have in common?

choices.text: They were directed by the Wachowskis (Cloud Atlas together with Tom Tykwer)
They have the same main actor
They both take place in a single day

content.explanation: Cloud Atlas, adapted from David Mitchell's novel, weaves six stories across several centuries, and the same actors play several roles in different stories.

content.question: Psycho, Vertigo and The Birds were all directed by...
content.explanation: Hitchcock, the "Master of Suspense", also appeared briefly in most of his own films: spotting his cameo is a game for his fans.

content.question: Which of these three Hitchcock films came out first?
content.explanation: Vertigo came out in 1958, Psycho in 1960 and The Birds in 1963.

content.question: In Psycho, where does the famous shower scene take place?
content.explanation: Marion Crane stops at the motel run by Norman Bates. The Overlook Hotel is in The Shining.

content.question: In Vertigo, what does the detective Scottie, played by James Stewart, suffer from?
content.explanation: His acrophobia is at the heart of the plot, set in San Francisco. For the dizzying shots, Hitchcock used a camera trick now called the "dolly zoom".

content.question: What attacks the small town of Bodega Bay in The Birds (1963)?
content.explanation: Yes, it is in the title! Hitchcock never explains why the birds attack, which makes the film even more unsettling.
